title: A digestion of the Jacobian conjecture counterexample
summary: Terence Tao provides an accessible explanation and analysis of a counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture, a famous unsolved problem in algebraic geometry that asks whether polynomial maps with nowhere-vanishing Jacobian determinants must be globally invertible.
problem_solved: Explains and digests why a polynomial map from C^n to C^n with non-vanishing Jacobian determinant fails to be globally invertible in certain cases, disproving the Jacobian conjecture.
why_valuable: Transforms a highly technical mathematical counterexample into an accessible digest, making advanced algebraic geometry concepts understandable to working mathematicians and advanced students.
